correctness.rationale: The proof starts with exact spectral/nuclear norm duality, derives joint concavity of matrix fidelity via a positive-definite variational minimum, and uses special-row/column Gram permutation invariance to certify that the two-mass stationary point is a global optimum even for nonsymmetric complex Hadamard matrices. A dephased two-dimensional invariant block produces the exact nuclear objective; its derivative has a unique positive zero for all n>=3, and tangency gives the stated radical. n=2,zeta=-1 is handled as a rank-one symbol. Strict phase ordering and quadratic deficit follow by h monotonicity and envelope differentiation. Numerical tests independently optimize unrestricted row/column weights for 39 finite complex Hadamard/phase examples with 117 local starts; all comparisons pass. These finite tests are supplementary, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The closest independently established special case is the exact sign-flip norm for a real Hadamard matrix (prior claim 3adaaaf0-d7ec-4495-a670-2490965d6d7c), itself generalizing a Walsh case (e51d2d78-1123-43a8-9084-964a70c58322). It is recovered only at phase -1. The assessed theorem treats all complex Hadamard orders, every unit phase, and derives strict phase ordering and a sharp local quadratic deficit; these latter statements are not implications of a single -1 value. Holbrook--Johnston--Schoch (arXiv:2206.02863v1) study real sign matrices and the global Hadamard bound, not the continuous complex-phase profile. Davidson--Donsig, Cowen et al., and Christensen supply general methods rather than this exact class formula. Targeted public searches and published mathematical database searches found no matching phase formula. Residual priority risk remains, especially under trace-fidelity or diagonal-scaling terminology.
residual_risks: Historical equality under diagonal-scaling/fidelity reparameterizations may appear in older matrix-analysis literature not discovered by targeted searches.
A general SDP characterization is known; novelty is confined to its evaluated phase-perturbation family, strict monotonicity and local coefficient.
Exact priority has not been independently verified; absent retrieval results are not proof of novelty.

value.rationale: The exact response of a maximal Schur-norm complex Hadamard symbol to the smallest unimodular entry perturbation is a natural stability invariant: it measures amplification under a phase error in a Fourier/Hadamard multiplier. The theorem covers all Fourier orders (including those with no real Hadamard), every complex Hadamard equivalence class, and a continuous phase parameter, and proves an unexpected class-independent strict ordering and a sharp local quadratic rigidity coefficient. These features are not determined by the known isolated -1 sign-flip norm and are relevant to understanding robustness of spectral Schur multipliers; no broader unrelated conjecture is claimed.
